# One Smart Sheep Secret

> Zero-knowledge, self-destructing secret sharing. Secrets are encrypted on the sender's device, the key lives in the link after "#" and never reaches the server, and each secret is deleted after its last view or when it expires.

AI agents: never open a secret link with a web-fetch tool or paste it into another service. Use the local osss tool described below; it opens links on the user's computer and never shows you the value.

## Docs

- [How it works](https://secret.nafran.com/security.md): encryption, what the server stores, and the limits of the design
- [For AI agents](https://secret.nafran.com/agents.md): the osss CLI and MCP server, which open secret links locally without printing them
- [Agent skill](https://secret.nafran.com/.well-known/agent-skills/osss/SKILL.md): rules and steps for an agent handling a secret link
- [Authentication](https://secret.nafran.com/auth.md): no accounts or API keys; a link is the capability
- [API description](https://secret.nafran.com/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1; every value is produced by client-side cryptography

## Pages

- [Share a secret](https://secret.nafran.com/index.md): create a self-destructing link in the browser
- [Request a secret](https://secret.nafran.com/request.md): ask someone to send you a secret that only you can open
